title: JMAP Chat has no language model: name/description/displayName/statusText/topic and message bodies carry no language, and clients can't ask for one
description:
Found 2026-11-14 while wiring mimid's JMAP Chat.name to MIMI room metadata (mimid bead mimid-1wgh.51), after a sweep of the MIMI drafts for English text that reaches users (IETF notes/2026-11-14-mimi-issues-from-table-draft.md, item 8).

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 says nothing about language anywhere. Human-readable properties with no language and no way to carry more than one:
- Chat: name (L599), description (L602), topic (L623, server-set)
- ChatContact: displayName (L525), statusText (L540)
- PresenceStatus: statusText (L1029)
- Space: name (L881), description (L884); Category: name (L847); SpaceRole: name (L799); CustomEmoji: name (L930)
- Endpoint and MessageAction label (L403, L426)
- Message: a body has bodyType but no language. MIMI content carries a per-part language (mimi-content-10), which a gateway drops; the rich body has a 'codeblock' lang (L1571) but that is a syntax hint, not the text's language.
Nor can a client say which language it wants (no request-side preference; JMAP has none generally).

Established pattern to reuse: JSCalendar RFC 8984 §4.2.8 locale (the language of the object's text) and §4.6.1 localizations (a map from language tag to PatchObject over the localizable properties), as used by JMAP Calendars. Proposal to work out:
1. Chat, Space, Category, SpaceRole, ChatContact, CustomEmoji gain optional locale and localizations.
2. Message gains an optional language (BCP 47) for the body, filled from mimi-content's part language by MIMI gateways.
3. Say whether a server MAY pick a localization for the client (e.g. from an account or session preference) or always returns all and lets the client choose. Prefer the latter (MAY, no MUST), in line with Mark's MAY > SHOULD > MUST preference.
4. Say that names are display text: servers and clients MUST NOT give them meaning (no matching on English role or space names), the same rule as proposed for MIMI room-policy.
Also check the companion drafts (mimi-00, federation-00, filenode-00) for the same gap.

Unblocks mimid-1wgh.51, which should implement whatever this settles rather than inventing an Accept-Language rule.
